   8class CellStyle(ABC):
   9    """Abstract base class for a cell style"""
  10
  11    def __init__(self):
  12        pass
  13
  14    def get_dict(self, property_name: str) -> Dict:
  15        """Get the dict representation of this cell style.
  16
  17        Args:
  18            property_name (str): The name of the property for which you want to define the cell style
  19
  20        Returns:
  21            Dict: dict representation of this cell style
  22        """
  23        result = {}
  24        for suffix, value in self._dict_suffixes.items():
  25            result[property_name + suffix] = value
  26        return result
  27
  28    @property
  29    @abstractmethod
  30    def _dict_suffixes(self) -> Dict:
  31        """Get the dict representation of the suffixes that need to be appended to the name of this property in this CellStyle object's dict representation.
  32
  33        Returns:
  34            Dict: the dict representation of the suffixes that need to be appended to the name of this property in this CellStyle object's dict representation
  35        """
  36        return {}
  37

 388class Element(ABC):
 389    """The abstract base class for elements."""
 390
 391    def __init__(self, name: str):
 392        """
 393        Args:
 394            name (str): The name of this element.
 395        """
 396        self.name = name
 397
 398    def __str__(self) -> str:
 399        """Get the string representation of this object.
 400
 401        Returns:
 402            str: string representation of this object
 403        """
 404        return self.json
 405
 406    def __repr__(self) -> str:
 407        """Get the JSON representation of this object.
 408
 409        Returns:
 410            str: JSON representation of this object
 411        """
 412        return self.json
 413
 414    @property
 415    def json(self) -> str:
 416        """JSON representation of this `Element`.
 417
 418        Isomorphic with the dict representation (`Element.as_dict`).
 419
 420        Returns:
 421            str: JSON representation
 422        """
 423        return json.dumps(self.as_dict)
 424
 425    @property
 426    @abstractmethod
 427    def as_dict(self) -> Dict:
 428        """Dictionary representation of this `Element`.
 429
 430        Isomorphic with the JSON representation (`Element.json`).
 431
 432        Returns:
 433            Dict: dictionary representation
 434        """
 435        pass
 436
 437    @property
 438    @abstractmethod
 439    def available_tags(self) -> FrozenSet[str]:
 440        """A `frozenset` containing all available template tags this `Element` reacts to.
 441
 442        Returns:
 443            FrozenSet[str]: set of tags associated with this `Element`
 444        """
 445        pass
 446
 447

 452class Property(Element):
 453    """The most basic `Element`. It simply consists of a name and a value.
 454
 455    In a template, `{name}` is replaced by `value`.
 456    """
 457
 458    def __init__(self, name: str, value: str):
 459        """
 460        Args:
 461            name (str): The name for this property.
 462            value (str): The value for this property. Note: the general purpose for this value-field is the value as a string,
 463                but this can be of any type, for example a dict.
 464        """
 465        super().__init__(name)
 466        self.value: Union[int, str] = value
 467
 468    @property
 469    def available_tags(self) -> FrozenSet[str]:
 470        return frozenset({"{" + self.name + "}"})
 471
 472    @property
 473    def as_dict(self) -> Dict:
 474        return {self.name: self.value}
 475

 477class CellStyleProperty(Property):
 478    def __init__(self, name: str, value: str, cell_style: CellStyle):
 479        """
 480        Args:
 481            name (str): The name for this property
 482            value (str): The value for this property
 483            cell_style (CellStyle): Cell style as a `CellStyle`.
 484        """
 485        super().__init__(name, value)
 486        self.cell_style: CellStyle = cell_style
 487
 488    @property
 489    def available_tags(self) -> FrozenSet[str]:
 490        return frozenset({"{" + self.name + "$}"})
 491
 492    @property
 493    def as_dict(self) -> Dict:
 494        result = {self.name: self.value}
 495
 496        for suffix, value in self.cell_style._dict_suffixes.items():
 497            result[self.name + suffix] = value
 498
 499        return result

 582class AutoLink(Property):
 583    """ This tag allows you to insert text into the document detecting links.
 584       For PPTX templates, additional styling options are available including:
 585    - Custom font color for hyperlinks
 586    - Custom underline color
 587    - Option to preserve template styling
 588    """
 589
 590    def __init__(self, 
 591                 name: str, 
 592                 value: str,
 593                 font_color: Union[str, None] = None,
 594                 underline_color: Union[str, None] = None,
 595                 preserve_tag_style: Union[bool, str, None] = None):
 596        """
 597        Args:
 598            name (str): The name for this element.
 599            value (str): The value of the autoLink.
 600            font_color (str, optional): PPTX-only The font color of autolink.
 601            underline_color (str, optional): The underline color of autolink.
 602            preserve_tag_style (str or bool, optional): Take the styling of hyperlink text defined in the template (blue and underlined by default).
 603        """
 604        super().__init__(name, value)
 605        self.value: str = value
 606        self.font_color = font_color
 607        self.underline_color = underline_color
 608        self.preserve_tag_style = preserve_tag_style
 609
 610    @property
 611    def available_tags(self) -> FrozenSet[str]:
 612        return frozenset({"{*auto " + self.name + "}"})
 613    @property
 614    def as_dict(self) -> Dict :
 615        result ={self.name:self.value}
 616        if self.font_color is not None:
 617            result[f"{self.name}_font_color"] = self.font_color
 618        if self.underline_color is not None:
 619            result[f"{self.name}_underline_color"] = self.underline_color
 620        if self.preserve_tag_style is not None:
 621            result[f"{self.name}_preserve_tag_style"] = self.preserve_tag_style
 622        return result
 623    
 624class Hyperlink(Element):

 626        """
 627        Args:
 628            name (str): The name for this element.
 629            url (str): The URL for the hyperlink.
 630            text (str, optional): The text for the hyperlink. Defaults to None.
 631            font_color (str, optional): PPTX ONLY -The font color of text for hyperlink. ( optional)
 632            underline_color (str, optional): PPTX ONLY -The underline color of text for hyperlink. ( optional)
 633            preserve_tag_style (str or bool, optional): For PPTX & Word- Take the styling of hyperlink text defined in the template (blue and underlined by default). ( optional)
 634        """
 635        super().__init__(name)
 636        self.url: str = url
 637        self.text: Union[str, None] = None
 638        self.font_color: Union[str, None] = None
 639        self.underline_color: Union[str, None] = None
 640        self.preserve_tag_style: Union[str, bool, None] = None
 641
 642    @property
 643    def available_tags(self) -> FrozenSet[str]:
 644        return frozenset({"{*" + self.name + "}"})
 645
 646    @property
 647    def as_dict(self) -> Dict:
 648        result = {self.name: self.url}
 649
 650        if self.text is not None:
 651            result[self.name + "_text"] = self.text
 652        if  (self.text is not None) and (self.font_color is not None):
 653            result[self.text + "_font_color"] = self.font_color
 654        if (self.text is not None) and (self.underline_color is not None):
 655            result[self.text + "_underline_color"] = self.underline_color
 656        if (self.preserve_tag_style is not None):
 657            result[self.name + "_preserve_tag_style"] = self.preserve_tag_style
 658
 659        return result

 925class COPChart(Element):
 926    """The class for an COPChart. This is used for chart templating."""
 927
 928    def __init__(
 929        self,
 930        name: str,
 931        x_data: Iterable[Union[str, int, float, Mapping]],
 932        y_datas: Union[
 933            Iterable[Iterable[Union[str, int, float, Mapping]]],
 934            Mapping[str, Iterable[Union[str, int, float, Mapping]]],
 935        ],
 936        date: COPChartDateOptions = None,
 937        title: str = None,
 938        x_title: str = None,
 939        y_title: str = None,
 940        y2_title: str = None,
 941        x2_title: str = None,
 942    ):
 943        """
 944        Args:
 945            name (str): The name for this element.
 946            x_data (Iterable[Union[str, int, float, Mapping]]): The data for the x-axis. Format : ["day 1", "day 2", "day 3", "day 4", "day 5"] or
 947                [{"value": "day 1"}, {"value": "day 2"}, {"value": "day 3"}, {"value": "day 4"}, {"value": "day 5"}]
 948            y_datas (Union[Iterable[Iterable[Union[str, int, float, Mapping]]], Mapping[str, Iterable[Union[str, int, float, Mapping]]]]):
 949                The data for the y-axis in the same format as x_data.
 950            date (COPChartDateOptions, optional): The date options for the chart. Defaults to None.
 951            title (str, optional): The title of the chart. Defaults to None.
 952            x_title (str, optional): The title for the x-axis. Defaults to None.
 953            y_title (str, optional): The title for the y-axis. Defaults to None.
 954            y2_title (str, optional): The title for the second y-axis. Defaults to None.
 955            x2_title (str, optional): The title for the second x-axis. Defaults to None.
 956
 957        Raises:
 958            TypeError: raise error when the input data for the y-axis is not valid
 959        """
 960        super().__init__(name)
 961        self.x_data: List = list(x_data)
 962
 963        self.y_datas: Dict[str, Iterable[Union[str, int, float]]] = None
 964        """If the argument 'y_datas' is of type Iterable[Iterable], then default names (e.g. series 1, series 2, ...) will be used."""
 965        if isinstance(y_datas, Mapping):
 966            self.y_datas = {name: list(data) for name, data in y_datas.items()}
 967        elif isinstance(y_datas, Iterable):
 968            self.y_datas = {
 969                f"series {i+1}": list(data) for i, data in enumerate(y_datas)
 970            }
 971        else:
 972            raise TypeError(
 973                f'Expected Mapping or Iterable for y_data, got "{type(y_datas)}"'
 974            )
 975
 976        self.date: COPChartDateOptions = date
 977        self.title: str = title
 978        self.x_title: str = x_title
 979        self.y_title: str = y_title
 980        self.x2_title: str = x2_title
 981        self.y2_title: str = y2_title
 982
 983    @classmethod
 984    def from_dataframe(
 985        cls,
 986        name: str,
 987        data: "pandas.DataFrame",
 988        date: COPChartDateOptions = None,
 989        title: str = None,
 990        x_title: str = None,
 991        y_title: str = None,
 992        y2_title: str = None,
 993        x2_title: str = None,
 994    ) -> "COPChart":
 995        """Construct an COPChart object from a [Pandas dataframe](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/reference/api/pandas.DataFrame.html).
 996
 997        Args:
 998            name (str): The name for this element.
 999            data (pandas.DataFrame): The data for this COPChart in a Pandas dataframe
1000            date (COPChartDateOptions, optional): The date options for the chart. Defaults to None.
1001            title (str, optional): The title for the chart. Defaults to None.
1002            x_title (str, optional): The title for the x-axis. Defaults to None.
1003            y_title (str, optional): The title for the y-axis. Defaults to None.
1004            y2_title (str, optional): The title for the second y-axis. Defaults to None.
1005            x2_title (str, optional): The title for the second x-axis. Defaults to None.
1006
1007        Returns:
1008            COPChart: the COPChart object generated from the dataframe
1009        """
1010        x_data = list(data.iloc[:, 0])
1011
1012        y_frame = data.iloc[:, 1:]
1013        y_datas = {}
1014        for col_name, col_data in y_frame.iteritems():
1015            y_datas[col_name] = col_data
1016
1017        return cls(
1018            name, x_data, y_datas, date, title, x_title, y_title, y2_title, x2_title
1019        )
1020
1021    @property
1022    def as_dict(self) -> Dict:
1023        result = {
1024            "xAxis": {
1025                "data": self.x_data,
1026            },
1027            "yAxis": {
1028                "series": [
1029                    {"name": name, "data": data} for name, data in self.y_datas.items()
1030                ]
1031            },
1032        }
1033
1034        if self.title is not None:
1035            result["title"] = self.title
1036        if self.date is not None:
1037            result["xAxis"]["date"] = self.date.as_dict
1038        if self.x_title is not None:
1039            result["xAxis"]["title"] = self.x_title
1040        if self.y_title is not None:
1041            result["yAxis"]["title"] = self.y_title
1042        if self.x2_title is not None:
1043            result["x2Axis"] = {}
1044            result["x2Axis"]["title"] = self.x2_title
1045        if self.y2_title is not None:
1046            result["y2Axis"] = {}
1047            result["y2Axis"]["title"] = self.y2_title
1048
1049        return {self.name: result}
1050
1051    @property
1052    def available_tags(self) -> FrozenSet[str]:
1053        return frozenset({"{aopchart " + self.name + "}"})
1054

1487class ValidateCell(Element):
1488    """
1489    It is possible to insert cell validation in excel using validate tag as {validate validateTag} (validate keyword followed by tagName)
1490    """
1491
1492    def __init__(self,
1493                 name: str,
1494                 ignoreBlank: bool = None,
1495                 allow: str = None,
1496                 value1: str = None,
1497                 value2: str = None,
1498                 inCellDropdown: bool = None,
1499                 data: str = None,
1500                 showInputMessage: bool = None,
1501                 inputTitle: str = None,
1502                 inputMessage: str = None,
1503                 showErrorAlert: bool = None,
1504                 errorStyle: str = None,
1505                 errorTitle: str = None,
1506                 errorMessage: str = None,
1507                 ):
1508        """Available option while using validate cell are ( ignoreBlank, allow, value1, value2, inCellDropdown, data, showInputMessage, inputTitle, inputMessage, showErrorAlert, errorStyle, errorTitle,errorMessage )
1509
1510        Args:
1511            name (string, optional): Name of the validate tag. For {validate tagName}, tagName is name for this element. 
1512            ignoreBlank (bool, optional): Set it to false for not allowing empty values in cell. The value is true by default.
1513            allow (string, optional): Type of data used for validation. Available options are (anyValue, whole, decimal, list, date, time, textLength, custom). Please use camelCase to insert value for allow attribute.
1514            value1 (string, optional): Value to compare with.
1515            value2 (string, optional): Value to compare with.<br>
1516            <i>Note:
1517                These two options <strong>(_value1, _value2)</strong> can be used for any allow/type of validation that require values for comparison, in such case use <strong>"_value1"</strong> attribute as the first value to be passed and <strong>"_value2"</strong> attribute as the 2nd value.<br><br>
1518                Some allow type of validation require only one value to compare; in such case use <strong>"_value1"</strong> attribute.<br><br>
1519                For ex :<br>
1520                If allow type of validation is date and you have to check in between two dates.<br>
1521                Then you could use <strong>"_value1"</strong> attribute as start date and <strong>"_value2"</strong> attribute as end date.<br><br>
1522                If allow type of validation is whole and you have to check for value less than 100.<br>
1523                Then you could use <strong>"_value1"</strong> for that value and do not use "<strong>_value2".</strong><br><br>
1524                While using time and date as allow type validation, please provide date/time with correct formatting.<br>
1525                for time: <strong>hours:minutes:seconds</strong> i.e hours , minutes, seconds separated by colon (:)<br>
1526                    ex : 14:30:00 for 2:30 pm<br><br>
1527                for date: <strong>month/day/year</strong> i.e day, month , year separated by forward slash(/)<br>
1528                    ex : 02/07/2023 for Feb 7 2023.<br><br>
1529                for list: you could use normal string with elements separated by comma(,).<br>
1530                    ex : "first, second, third" for list of three elements.<br></i>
1531            inCellDropdown (bool, optional): Set it to false for not showing dropdown button while validation allow type is list. It is true by default for list allow type.
1532            data (string, optional): Type of comparison to be done for the cell value. Available values are (lessThanOrEqual, notBetween, equal, notEqual, greaterThan, greaterThan, lessThan, greaterThanOrEqual, lessThanOrEqual). Default value is "between". Please use camelCase for the value as shown in examples.
1533            showInputMessage (bool, optional): Set it to false to hide message shown when the cell to validate is being selected. The value for it is true by default.
1534            inputTitle (string, optional): Title of message to be shown when cell to validate is selected.
1535            inputMessage (string, optional): Message to be shown when cell to validate is selected.
1536            showErrorAlert (bool, optional): Set it to false, if you want to hide error alert once cell validation fails. The value is true by default.
1537            errorStyle (string, optional): Type of error style when cell validation fails. The value is stop by default. Available options are(stop,waring, Information).
1538            errorTitle (string, optional): Title of error to be shown when cell validation fails.
1539            errorMessage (string, optional): Message of error to be shown when cell validation fails.
1540        """
1541        super().__init__(name)
1542        self.ignoreBlank = ignoreBlank
1543        self.allow = allow
1544        self.value1 = value1
1545        self.value2 = value2
1546        self.inCellDropdown = inCellDropdown
1547        self.data = data
1548        self.showInputMessage = showInputMessage
1549        self.inputTitle = inputTitle
1550        self.inputMessage = inputMessage
1551        self.showErrorAlert = showErrorAlert
1552        self.errorStyle = errorStyle
1553        self.errorTitle = errorTitle
1554        self.errorMessage = errorMessage
1555
1556    @property
1557    def available_tags(self) -> FrozenSet[str]:
1558        return frozenset({"{validate " + self.name + "}"})
1559
1560    @property
1561    def as_dict(self) -> Dict:
1562        result = {}
1563        if self.ignoreBlank is not None:
1564            result[self.name + '_ignore_blank'] = self.ignoreBlank
1565        if self.allow is not None:
1566            result[self.name + '_allow'] = self.allow
1567        if self.value1 is not None:
1568            result[self.name + '_value1'] = self.value1
1569        if self.value2 is not None:
1570            result[self.name + '_value2'] = self.value2
1571        if self.inCellDropdown is not None:
1572            result[self.name + '_in_cell_dropdown'] = self.inCellDropdown
1573        if self.data is not None:
1574            result[self.name + '_data'] = self.data
1575        if self.showInputMessage is not None:
1576            result[self.name + '_show_input_message'] = self.showInputMessage
1577        if self.inputTitle is not None:
1578            result[self.name + '_input_title'] = self.inputTitle
1579        if self.inputMessage is not None:

1592class Link(Property):
1593    """The class for the link/target tags.
1594    This tags allows you to place a link to a target in the same document.
1595    If the uid is not provided, a new uid will be generated uniquely for every link and target pair.
1596    """
1597
1598    def __init__(
1599        self,
1600        name: str,
1601        value: str,
1602        uid_name: str = None,
1603        uid_value: str = None,
1604    ):
1605        """Create a new link/target tag pair.
1606        If the uid is not provided, a new uid will be generated uniquely for each link/target pair.
1607
1608        Args:
1609            name (str): the name of the link/target tags.
1610            value (str): the value of the link/target tags.
1611            uid_name (str): the name of the uid of the link/target pair.
1612            uid_value (str): the value of the uid of the link/target pair.
1613        """
1614        super().__init__(name, value)
1615        self.uid_name = uid_name
1616        self.uid_value = uid_value
1617
1618    @property
1619    def available_tags(self) -> FrozenSet[str]:
1620        if self.uid_name and self.uid_value:
1621            return frozenset(
1622                {
1623                    "{link" + self.name + ":" + self.uid_name + "}",
1624                    "{target" + self.name + ":" + self.uid_name + "}",
1625                }
1626            )
1627        return frozenset({"{link" + self.name + "}", "{target" + self.name + "}"})
1628
1629    @property
1630    def as_dict(self) -> Dict:
1631        if self.uid_name and self.uid_value:
1632            return {self.name: self.value, self.uid_name: self.uid_value}
1633        return {self.name: self.value}

1636class ElementCollection(list, Element):
1637    """A collection used to group multiple elements together.
1638    It can contain nested `ElementCollection`s and should be used to pass multiple `Element`s as PrintJob data, as well as to allow for nested elements.
1639    Its name is used as a key name when nested, but ignored for all purposes when it's the outer ElementCollection.
1640    """
1641
1642    def __init__(self, name: str = "", elements: Iterable[Element] = ()):
1643        """
1644        Args:
1645            name (str, optional): The name for this element collection. Not used for the outer ElementCollection, but needed for nested ElementCollections Defaults to "".
1646            elements (Iterable[Element], optional): An iterable containing the elements that need to be added to this collection. Defaults to ().
1647        """
1648        list.__init__(self, elements)
1649        Element.__init__(self, name)
1650
1651    def __str__(self) -> str:
1652        """
1653        Returns:
1654            str: The string representation for this object.
1655        """
1656        return self.json
1657
1658    def __repr__(self) -> str:
1659        """
1660        Returns:
1661            str: The JSON representation for this object.
1662        """
1663        return self.json
1664
1665    def copy(self) -> "ElementCollection":
1666        """
1667        Returns:
1668            ElementCollection: A copy of this element collection.
1669        """
1670        return self.__class__(self)
1671
1672    def deepcopy(self) -> "ElementCollection":
1673        """
1674        Returns:
1675            ElementCollection: A deep copy of this element collection.
1676        """
1677        return deepcopy(self)
1678
1679    @property
1680    def json(self):
1681        return json.dumps(self.as_dict)
1682
1683    def add(self, element: Element):
1684        """Add an element to this element collection object.
1685
1686        Args:
1687            element (Element): the element to add to this collection
1688        """
1689        self.append(element)
1690
1691    def add_all(self, obj: "ElementCollection"):
1692        """Add all the elements in the given collection to this collection.
1693
1694        Args:
1695            obj (ElementCollection): the collection of which the elements need to be added to this element collection object
1696        """
1697        for element in obj:
1698            self.add(element)
1699
1700    def remove_element_by_name(self, element_name: str):
1701        """Remove an element from this element collection object by its name.
1702
1703        Args:
1704            element_name (str): the name of the element that needs to be removed
1705        """
1706        self.remove(
1707            next(element for element in self if element.name == element_name))
1708
1709    @property
1710    def as_dict(self) -> Dict:
1711        """Merge the `ElementCollection`'s contents as one dict.
1712
1713        Returns:
1714            Dict: merged element
1715        """
1716        result = {}
1717        for element in self:
1718            if isinstance(element, ElementCollection):
1719                result.update({element.name: element.as_dict})
1720            elif isinstance(element, FormElement):
1721                result.setdefault(element.name, []).append(element.as_dict)
1722            else:
1723                result.update(element.as_dict)
1724        return result
1725
1726    @property
1727    def available_tags(self) -> FrozenSet[str]:
1728        result = set()
1729        for element in self:
1730            result |= element.available_tags
1731        return frozenset(result)
1732
1733    @classmethod
1734    def element_to_element_collection(
1735        cls, element: Element, name: str = ""
1736    ) -> "ElementCollection":
1737        """Generate an element collection from an element and a name.
1738
1739        Args:
1740            element (Element): the element that needs to be transformed to an element collection
1741            name (str): The name of the element collection. Defaults to ''.
1742
1743        Returns:
1744            ElementCollection: the generated element collection from an element and a name
1745        """
1746        return cls.from_mapping(element.as_dict, name)
1747
1748    @classmethod
1749    def from_mapping(cls, mapping: Mapping, name: str = "") -> "ElementCollection":
1750        """Generate an element collection from a mapping and a name.
1751
1752        Args:
1753            mapping (Mapping): the mapping that needs to be converted to an element collection
1754            name (str): The name of the element collection. Defaults to ''.
1755
1756        Returns:
1757            ElementCollection: an element collection generated from the given mapping and name
1758        """
1759        result_set = set()
1760        for key, value in mapping.items():
1761            result_set.add(Property(key, value))
1762        return cls(name, result_set)
1763
1764    @classmethod
1765    def from_json(cls, json_str: str, name: str = "") -> "ElementCollection":
1766        """Generate an element collection from a JSON string.
1767
1768        Args:
1769            json_str (str): the json string that needs to be transformed to an element collection
1770            name (str): The name of the element collection. Defaults to ''.
1771
1772        Returns:
1773            ElementCollection: an element collection generated from the given JSON string and name
1774        """
1775        return cls.from_mapping(json.loads(json_str), name)

584    """ This tag allows you to insert text into the document detecting links.
585       For PPTX templates, additional styling options are available including:

587    - Custom underline color
588    - Option to preserve template styling

592                 name: str, 
593                 value: str,

598        Args:
599            name (str): The name for this element.
600            value (str): The value of the autoLink.
601            font_color (str, optional): PPTX-only The font color of autolink.
602            underline_color (str, optional): The underline color of autolink.
603            preserve_tag_style (str or bool, optional): Take the styling of hyperlink text defined in the template (blue and underlined by default).
604        """
605        super().__init__(name, value)
606        self.value: str = value
607        self.font_color = font_color
608        self.underline_color = underline_color
609        self.preserve_tag_style = preserve_tag_style

613        return frozenset({"{*auto " + self.name + "}"})

619        if self.underline_color is not None:
620            result[f"{self.name}_underline_color"] = self.underline_color
621        if self.preserve_tag_style is not None:
622            result[f"{self.name}_preserve_tag_style"] = self.preserve_tag_style
623        return result

1511        Args:
1512            name (string, optional): Name of the validate tag. For {validate tagName}, tagName is name for this element.

1515            value1 (string, optional): Value to compare with.
1516            value2 (string, optional): Value to compare with.<br>
1517            <i>Note:
1518                These two options <strong>(_value1, _value2)</strong> can be used for any allow/type of validation that require values for comparison, in such case use <strong>"_value1"</strong> attribute as the first value to be passed and <strong>"_value2"</strong> attribute as the 2nd value.<br><br>
1519                Some allow type of validation require only one value to compare; in such case use <strong>"_value1"</strong> attribute.<br><br>
1520                For ex :<br>
1521                If allow type of validation is date and you have to check in between two dates.<br>
1522                Then you could use <strong>"_value1"</strong> attribute as start date and <strong>"_value2"</strong> attribute as end date.<br><br>
1523                If allow type of validation is whole and you have to check for value less than 100.<br>
1524                Then you could use <strong>"_value1"</strong> for that value and do not use "<strong>_value2".</strong><br><br>
1525                While using time and date as allow type validation, please provide date/time with correct formatting.<br>
1526                for time: <strong>hours:minutes:seconds</strong> i.e hours , minutes, seconds separated by colon (:)<br>
1527                    ex : 14:30:00 for 2:30 pm<br><br>
1528                for date: <strong>month/day/year</strong> i.e day, month , year separated by forward slash(/)<br>
1529                    ex : 02/07/2023 for Feb 7 2023.<br><br>
1530                for list: you could use normal string with elements separated by comma(,).<br>
1531                    ex : "first, second, third" for list of three elements.<br></i>
1532            inCellDropdown (bool, optional): Set it to false for not showing dropdown button while validation allow type is list. It is true by default for list allow type.
1533            data (string, optional): Type of comparison to be done for the cell value. Available values are (lessThanOrEqual, notBetween, equal, notEqual, greaterThan, greaterThan, lessThan, greaterThanOrEqual, lessThanOrEqual). Default value is "between". Please use camelCase for the value as shown in examples.

1535            inputTitle (string, optional): Title of message to be shown when cell to validate is selected.
1536            inputMessage (string, optional): Message to be shown when cell to validate is selected.

1539            errorTitle (string, optional): Title of error to be shown when cell validation fails.
1540            errorMessage (string, optional): Message of error to be shown when cell validation fails.
1541        """
